title: The Night Went Gray
body: Once, the town slept under a silver moon.
Then one night, the moon went soft and gray. Bedroom windows glowed, but the sky did not. A child hugged a pillow and whispered,
“Mom… the moon looks tired.”
High on a stone ledge, a tiny firefly named Pip watched the faded sky. Her own glow was only a honey-colored speck.
“If the moon can’t shine,” Pip said, “what chance do I have?”
She lifted off into the dark — one small spark in a big quiet town.

title: Rook and the Balloon Rocket
body: Clank. String. Scrap metal.
In a junkyard workshop, a raccoon named Rook wrestled a balloon rocket made of patches and hope.
“Almost— whoa!”
The rocket tipped. Pip steadied it with her tiny light.
“Hey,” Rook said. “Tiny flashlight with wings.”
“I’m Pip. The moon forgot how to glow. Kids can’t sleep.”
Rook grinned. “Then we go get it. I’ve got a rocket. You’ve got spark.”
“It’s a small spark,” Pip said.
“Small sparks start big nights,” Rook answered. “Climb in.”
They launched into the gray night.

title: The Cloud Maze
body: Soft blue clouds twisted into a maze. The rocket bumped and spun.
“I can’t see the path!” Rook cried.
Pip flew ahead. Her light painted a golden trail through the fog.
“This way… left… now straight!”
They burst out above the clouds. Pip looked surprised she had led.
“See?” Rook said. “Small light. Big path.”

title: The Owl Who Kept the Shine
body: On a cloud nest sat a round Owl, buried in stolen sparkles and stars.
“Mine. All shiny. Mine.”
“We need a little glow for the moon,” Rook said.
“The moon can get a night-light,” the Owl sniffed, “like everyone else.”
Pip’s glow flickered — then steadied.
“Keeping light doesn’t make more light,” she said. “Sharing does.”
She offered one tiny spark. The Owl hesitated… then dropped a single star into her hands.
“…One,” he grumbled. “And bring it back if the moon’s rude.”

title: Dark Luma
body: They found Luma, Earth’s moon, sitting on a cloud like a cold stone — charcoal, dim, almost no light at all. One soft tear shone on her cheek.
“Everyone looks up for light,” Luma whispered. “Tonight I have none.”
“Then we’ll fix you,” Pip promised.
Luma stayed dark.
